name: Maughold

attributes.attribute: a Manx legendary figure also called St. Maughold or Machutus
converted by St. Patrick and set adrift in a padlocked boat
unlocked years later when a fish contained the lost key
rose to become bishop of the Isle of Man

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Maughold, also called St. Maughold or Machutus, was a Manx legendary figure. Early Christian legend on the Isle of Man says that St. Patrick converted him. Maughold was padlocked to a small boat and put out to sea. The key was thrown overboard, where a fish ate it. Maughold was rescued, but the lock could never be opened. Many years later, a fish was caught and served to him. The fish proved to contain the long-lost key. Unlocked at last, Maughold rose to become bishop of the island. The folkloric motifs in the story, and the feast of Maughold at the Celtic harvest holiday of Lughnasa, suggest that a Christian legend absorbed an earlier pagan one.

okr.objective: Document Maughold, the Manx saint and legendary bishop of the Isle of Man.
